Dyadic-flow dual bound and coarea bound on level bands

16 October 2026 · Working proof; in the dyadic flow's smearing · Flow and coarea. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: A bound in the dyadic flow's smearing on level bands; the goal's state in Where we stand is unchanged.

Question. The fifth route review's decisive test asks for a bound on nested chains of unions of cells charged by their local gaps, the obstacle being that the coarea bound loses \((\log N/\log y)^{1/4}\) at levels with \(\log y=o(\log N)\). The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy; this entry first takes the plainest available bound at low levels, the record's own dyadic flow, which bounds the class through its dual, and asks what it gives against the coarea bound. The proposed next step named queue item entry-2026-10-16-fourth-route-review:2 for this test; the entry develops no queue item, since the plainest bound came first, and that item's named attempt remains owed to it.

Target form. The goal's form is the class bound for cell-smeared measures; the working form is the class bound for the smearing of thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential's proof (\(X\) over dyadic cells of side \(\delta=2^{-J}\in[s/64,s/32]\), evenly spread \(Y\) over their rectangles, so \(\nu_Y=N\) times Lebesgue), which lem:flow-matching-bound (1) turns into matchings as the reduction does; it adds the restriction to functions whose larger partial stays between two levels.

General statement. lem:flow-coarea-level-bound: part (a) for every Lipschitz function, (b) for every class function at every pair in \([2,\infty]^2\), (c) and (d) at \((4,4)\) for every class function whose larger partial stays in \([y,Y]\), \(e^{16}\le y\le Y\).

Flow–coarea level bound

Statement. Let \(L\ge L_0\) of thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential, \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(\nu_X,\nu_Y\) the smearings of its proof, and \(\Phi\) its dyadic flow, with \(\int\nabla g\cdot\Phi=\int g\,d(\nu_X-\nu_Y)\) for every Lipschitz \(g\). With probability tending to one: (a) for every Lipschitz \(G\), \(|\int G\,d(\nu_X-\nu_Y)|\le\frac L4\sqrt{N\log N}(1+\sum_j\int\psi_2^*(|\partial_jG|))\); (b) for every exponent pair \(\alpha\in[2,\infty]^2\) and every Lipschitz \(G\) with \(\int\sum_j\psi^*_{\alpha_j}(|\partial_jG|)\le2\) and partials bounded by \(Y\), the right side of (a) is at most \(\frac L4\sqrt{N\log N}(23+6\max_j(\log\max\{Y,e^{16}\})^{1/2-1/\alpha_j})\); (c) at \((4,4)\), for every such \(G\) whose larger partial is at least \(y\ge e^{16}\) where \(\nabla G\ne0\) (no bound \(Y\) needed), \(|\int G\,d(\nu_X-\nu_Y)|\le L'\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}(\log y)^{-1/4}\), \(L'\) depending only on \(L\); (d) so at \((4,4)\), for \(G\) with larger partial in \([y,Y]\) where \(\nabla G\ne0\), the discrepancy is at most \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\min\{1+(\log Y)^{1/4},(\log N/\log y)^{1/4}\}\); when \(\log Y\le K\log y\) this is at most \(C_K\sqrt{N\log N}(\log N)^{1/8}\); when \(Y\le(\log N)^K\), (b) alone gives \(C_K\sqrt{N\log N}(\log\log N)^{1/4}\). Part (a) is the Fenchel–Young step of the proof of lem:flow-matching-bound (2), with \(C\) the \((2,2)\) cost at scale \(s\), applied to the event of thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential's proof; what this lemma adds is (b)–(d).

Proof. Event: the proof of thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential shows, on an event of probability tending to one ("Fine levels", with \(\eta\le1/8\)), \(I=\int_\Omega\psi_2(4|\Phi|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\le\frac12\), where \(L\sqrt{N\log N}=Ns\). (a) For \(t>0\) and \(u,v\ge0\), \(uv=t\,u\,(v/t)\le t(\psi_2(u)+\psi_2^*(v/t))\) (Young). With \(u=4|\Phi_j|/(Ns)\), \(v=s|\partial_jG|\), \(t=s\): \(|\partial_jG||\Phi_j|=\frac N4uv\le\frac{Ns}4(\psi_2(4|\Phi_j|/(Ns))+\psi_2^*(|\partial_jG|))\). Summing over \(j\), integrating, and using \(|\Phi_j|\le|\Phi|\), \(\psi_2\) increasing: \(|\int G\,d(\nu_X-\nu_Y)|=|\int\nabla G\cdot\Phi|\le\frac{Ns}4(2I+\sum_j\int\psi_2^*(|\partial_jG|))\), which is (a). (b) Conjugate bounds: \(\psi_2^*(a)=\sup_t(at-e^{t^2}+1)\); for \(a\ge0.29\), with \(t_0=\sqrt{\log(1+a)}\ge\frac12\), the derivative \(a-2te^{t^2}\) is negative beyond \(t_0\), so \(\psi_2^*(a)\le at_0=a\sqrt{\log(1+a)}\); for \(a<0.29\), \(e^{t^2}-1\ge t^2\) gives \(\psi_2^*(a)\le a^2/4<0.021\). For finite \(\alpha\ge2\) and \(a\ge e^{16}\), \(t=(\frac12\log a)^{1/\alpha}\) gives \(\psi_\alpha^*(a)\ge a(\frac12\log a)^{1/\alpha}-\sqrt a+1\ge\frac12a(\frac12\log a)^{1/\alpha}\ge\frac1{2\sqrt2}a(\log a)^{1/\alpha}\); for \(\alpha=\infty\), \(\psi_\infty^*(a)=a\) (\(a\le N\)); and \(t=1\) gives \(\psi^*_\alpha(a)\ge a-(e-1)\) for all \(a\). So, with \(\log(1+a)\le1.01\log a\) for \(a\ge e^{16}\): where \(a=|\partial_jG|\ge e^{16}\), \(\psi_2^*(a)\le2.85(\log a)^{1/2-1/\alpha_j}\psi^*_{\alpha_j}(a)\le2.85(\log\max\{Y,e^{16}\})^{1/2-1/\alpha_j}\psi^*_{\alpha_j}(a)\); where \(a<e^{16}\), \(\psi_2^*(a)\le4.01a+0.021\le4.01(\psi^*_{\alpha_j}(a)+1.72)+0.021\). Summing over \(j\) with \(\sum_j\int\psi^*_{\alpha_j}\le2\) and area one: \(\sum_j\int\psi_2^*(|\partial_jG|)\le5.7\max_j(\log\max\{Y,e^{16}\})^{1/2-1/\alpha_j}+8.02+13.84\), and \(1+\dots\le23+6\max_j(\dots)\). (c) \(\nu_X\) spreads each \(X_i\) uniformly over its level-\(J\) cell and \(\nu_Y=N\) times Lebesgue, so \(\int G\,d(\nu_X-\nu_Y)=\sum_i(E_JG)(X_i)-N\int E_JG\), \(E_JG\) the cell averages. The cell side \(\delta=2^{-J}\ge s/64=\frac L{64}\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \(\delta\le s/32\le2^{-\ell_1}\) for large \(N\), so lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) with \(\kappa=L/64\) gives \(L_\kappa\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}(E_JG)\); the translation sweep, the argument of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy's corollary carried out here at mesh \(\delta\), bounds \(\mathrm{TV}(E_JG)\le2\int(|\partial_1G|+|\partial_2G|)\), the variation counted as the sum over inner edges of \(\delta\) times the jump: for horizontally adjacent cells \(Q\) and \(Q'=Q+\delta e_1\), \(E_JG(Q')-E_JG(Q)=\delta^{-2}\int_Q\int_0^\delta\partial_1G(x+re_1)\,dr\,dx\), so \(\delta|E_JG(Q')-E_JG(Q)|\le\int_{Q\cup Q'}|\partial_1G|\), each cell lies in at most two horizontal pairs, and likewise vertically; and, as in lem:dominant-level-split, where \(\nabla G\ne0\) the larger partial \(t\ge y\ge e^{16}\) has \(|\partial_1G|+|\partial_2G|\le2t\le4\psi_4^*(t)(\log y)^{-1/4}\), so \(\int(|\partial_1G|+|\partial_2G|)\le8(\log y)^{-1/4}\); the bound \(Y\) is not used. (d) Both bounds hold on the intersection of the events; at \((4,4)\), \(\frac12-\frac14=\frac14\), and \(\min\{(\log Y)^{1/4},(\log N/\log y)^{1/4}\}\le(\log N)^{1/8}K^{1/8}\) when \(\log Y\le K\log y\) (the product of the two is at most \((K\log N)^{1/4}\)); when \(Y\le(\log N)^K\), \((\log Y)^{1/4}\le(K\log\log N)^{1/4}\), so there (b) alone gives the bound, without (c). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. \(L\ge L_0\): the event \(I\le\frac12\) of the dyadic flow's proof. The smearing \((\nu_X,\nu_Y)\): the flow's divergence identity, and in (c) the identity with the cell averages (\(\nu_Y\) Lebesgue). Partials bounded by \(Y\): only in (b), to replace \((\log a)^{1/2-1/\alpha}\) by its maximum; (a) holds for every Lipschitz \(G\), and (c) does not use \(Y\). The class budget \(\int\sum_j\psi^*_{\alpha_j}\le2\): (b) and (c). Exponents \(\alpha_j\ge2\): \((\frac12)^{1/\alpha}\ge\frac1{\sqrt2}\) in the conjugate bound of (b). Larger partial at least \(y\ge e^{16}\) in (c): the lower bound \(\psi_4^*(t)\ge\frac12t(\log t)^{1/4}\) used in lem:dominant-level-split. \(\kappa=L/64\) and large \(N\): lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor's side range in (c). The sweep in (c) is deterministic and holds at every mesh. Conclusions: (a) for every Lipschitz function; (b) for every class function at every pair in \([2,\infty]^2\); (c) at \((4,4)\) for the class functions of level at least \(y\); (d) for those of level in \([y,Y]\); all in this smearing, both signs of the discrepancy.

Baseline. Neither is shown tight.

Degenerate cases. \(G\) constant: both sides vanish. \(y=Y\): the strictly single-level case, both bounds apply. \(Y<e^{16}\): (b) is stated with \(\max\{Y,e^{16}\}\) and gives \(\frac L4\sqrt{N\log N}(23+6\cdot16^{1/2})\), the conjectured order; (c) and (d) exclude it by \(y\ge e^{16}\). A pair with an infinite exponent: the factor \((\log Y)^{1/2}\), where (b) is weakest.

Nonvacuity. On the curve's parameters at \((4,4)\), a ramp at level \(y\), \(Y=2y\), with \(y=(\log N)^2\) (the obstacle's level, where (b) alone decides) and with \(y=e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\) (the band where (c) and (b) are both of order \((\log N)^{1/8}\), so both are exercised): \(G(x_1,x_2)=a\min\{1,\max\{0,(x_2-x_1/2-\frac14)/w\}\}\) on the square, a ramp along a line of slope \(\frac12\), with \(w=a/y\) and \(a=\frac14(\log(1+2y))^{-1/4}\): its partials are \(\partial_2G=y\), \(\partial_1G=-y/2\) on the ramp, so the larger partial is \(y\in[y,Y]\), the ramp region \(\{0\le x_2-x_1/2-\frac14\le w\}\) has area \(w\), and the cost is \(w(\psi_4^*(y)+\psi_4^*(y/2))\le1.5\,wy(\log(1+y))^{1/4}=1.5a(\log(1+y))^{1/4}\le0.375\) (by \(\psi_4^*(x)\le x(\log(1+x))^{1/4}\)); \(y\ge e^{16}\) once \(\log N\ge e^8\) in the first case and \(\log N\ge256\) in the second. With probability tending to one, (d) gives \(C\sqrt{N\log N}(\log\log N)^{1/4}\) in the first case, by (b), and \(C\sqrt{N\log N}(\log N)^{1/8}\) in the second, where (b) gives \((23+6(\sqrt{\log N}+\log2)^{1/4})\) and (c) \((\log N)^{1/8}\), up to constants. Plainest bound. For one fixed ramp, a function of \(x_2-x_1/2\): the unsmeared sum is \(O(a\sqrt N)\) by a change of variables and the Dvoretzky–Kiefer–Wolfowitz inequality, and the smearing changes it by \(\sum_i(E_JG-G)(X_i)\), a centred sum (the cells partition the square) of at most \(N(w+3\delta)\) expected nonzero terms (the cells meeting the ramp) bounded by \(2\delta y\), of standard deviation \(O(\sqrt{Nwy^2\delta^2})=O(\sqrt{ay\log N})\), so \(O(\sqrt N)\) in both cases; the lemma's content is the uniformity over the class with level in \([y,Y]\), where the coarea bound of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor alone gives \((\log N/(2\log\log N))^{1/4}\) in the first case and \((\log N)^{1/8}\) in the second.

Dyadic flow edge fluxes bound the discrete class

17 October 2026 · Working proof; X-term, dyadic grids · Discrete flow. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: A bound for the discrete class's X-term on dyadic grids at capped increment levels; the goal's state in Where we stand is unchanged.

Question. The flow–coarea level bound bounded continuous class functions in the dyadic flow's smearing and left the fifth route review's outcome (B) untouched: (B) is about the discrete class, grid functions on cells of side \(\delta_0\) against the centred counts, where the transfer from Lipschitz functions was not shown. The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy; this entry asks whether the dyadic flow bounds the discrete class directly, through the fluxes across cell edges, and what that decides about (B).

Target form. The goal's form is the class bound for the cell-smeared \(\mu_X-\mu_Y\); the working form is its \(X\)-term in the discrete class of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor and the sample-point pyramids entry, \(D(g)=\sum_Q(n_Q-N\delta_0^2)g_Q\) for grid functions \(g\) on the cells of side \(\delta_0\) with the edge cost \(\sum_e\delta_0^2\psi^*_{\alpha_{d(e)}}(|\Delta_eg|/(2\delta_0))\le2\), \(d(e)\) the direction across \(e\); it adds a dyadic \(\delta_0\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\), one sequence \(\delta_0(N)\), and leaves the \(Y\)-term aside.

Chosen. The chaining lead entry-2026-10-16-fourth-route-review:2, not the queue head sandpile-odometer-flow: it bears directly on conjugate-class-discrepancy, its latest follow-up names the discrete class at level \((\log N)^2\), and the fifth route review's outcome (B) sits there.

General statement. lem:discrete-flow-bound: part (a) for every grid function, (b) for every discrete class function at every pair in \([2,\infty]^2\), (c) at \((4,4)\) for the grid functions with increments in \(\{0\}\cup[y\delta_0,Y\delta_0]\).

Discrete flow bound

Statement. Let \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) be i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\), \(L_0\) the constant of thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential, and \(\delta_0=\delta_0(N)=2^{-J}\) dyadic with \(\delta_0\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\). For a function \(g\) on the cells \(Q\) of side \(\delta_0\) write \(n_Q\) for the number of points in \(Q\), \(D(g)=\sum_Q(n_Q-N\delta_0^2)g_Q\), and \(\Delta_eg=g_{Q'}-g_Q\) for an inner edge \(e\) between \(Q\) and the next cell \(Q'\) in a coordinate direction. With probability tending to one: (a) every \(g\) has \[|D(g)|\le\tfrac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}\Big(1+\sum_e\delta_0^2\psi_2^*\big(|\Delta_eg|/\delta_0\big)\Big);\] (b) for every pair \(\alpha\in[2,\infty]^2\) and every \(g\) with \(\sum_e\delta_0^2\psi^*_{\alpha_{d(e)}}(|\Delta_eg|/(2\delta_0))\le2\) and \(|\Delta_eg|\le Y\delta_0\) on every edge, \(|D(g)|\le\frac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}\,(47+12\max_j(\log\max\{Y,2e^{16}\})^{1/2-1/\alpha_j})\); (c) at \((4,4)\), if moreover \(\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\) and every increment has \(|\Delta_eg|/\delta_0\in\{0\}\cup[y,Y]\) with \(2e^{16}\le y\le Y\), then \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}\min\{1+(\log Y)^{1/4},(\log N/\log(y/2))^{1/4}\}\), \(C\) universal; in particular every \(g=y\delta_0\sum_{k\le K}1_{A_k}\) with nested unions of cells \(A_1\supseteq\dots\supseteq A_K\), each inner edge on at most \(m\) of the boundaries \(\partial A_k\), and cost at most \(2\) has \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}(1+(\log(my))^{1/4})\), which for \(m\le2\) (the fifth review's chains) and \(y=(\log N)^2\) is at most \(C'\sqrt{N\log N}(\log\log N)^{1/4}\).

Proof. The flow. Let \(\Phi=\sum_{j<J}\Phi_j\) be the dyadic flow of thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential's proof, built down to level \(J\) of this \(\delta_0\). That proof uses the level \(J\) only through \(N4^{-J}\ge16\log N\) (the Chernoff event \(E_1\) on all squares of level at most \(J\)) and \(J\le\log N\) (the variance sum \(V=8NJ\le8N\log N\)); both hold here, so on an event of probability tending to one \(I:=\int\psi_2(4|\Phi|/(L_0\sqrt{N\log N}))\le\frac12\). Structure on a cell. By the construction of the square flows (#entry-2026-10-16-dyadic-flow-bound, the square-flow lemma's proof), \(\Phi^S=V+H\) with \(V=(0,v(y))\), \(v\) continuous and piecewise linear in \(y\) with its break on the horizontal midline of \(S\), and \(H=(k_b(x),0)\) on the half \(b\), \(k_b\) continuous and piecewise linear in \(x\) with its break on the vertical midline, both vanishing on \(\partial S\) in their normal direction. The midlines of a square of level \(j<J\) are grid lines of level \(j+1\le J\), so on every cell \(Q\) of side \(\delta_0\), \(\Phi^1=\phi_Q(x)\) is affine in \(x\) and independent of \(y\), \(\Phi^2=\chi_Q(y)\) affine in \(y\) and independent of \(x\); \(\Phi^1\) is continuous in \(x\) across vertical edges and \(\Phi^2\) in \(y\) across horizontal ones, and \(\Phi\cdot n=0\) on \(\partial[0,1]^2\). On the open cell \(Q\), the same proof's integration by parts gives \(-\operatorname{div}\Phi=\sum_{j<J}e_{c_j}/|S_{c_j}|\), the children \(S_{c_j}\supseteq Q\), which telescopes to \(n_Q/\delta_0^2-N\) (the record's identity \(\int\nabla g\cdot\Phi=\int g\,d(\nu_X-\nu_Y)\) with \(\nu_X\) of density \(n_Q/\delta_0^2\) on \(Q\) and \(\nu_Y=N\) times Lebesgue). Summation by parts. For a vertical edge \(e\) at \(x=x_e\) between \(Q\) and \(Q'\) put \(F_e=\int_e\Phi^1\,dy=\delta_0\phi_Q(x_e)\), and likewise for horizontal edges. By the divergence theorem on each cell, \(n_Q-N\delta_0^2=-\oint_{\partial Q}\Phi\cdot n\), so \(D(g)=-\sum_Qg_Q\oint_{\partial Q}\Phi\cdot n=\sum_eF_e\Delta_eg\), each inner edge contributing \(-g_QF_e+g_{Q'}F_e\) and the outer edges nothing. Edge bound. For an affine \(\phi\) on an interval of length \(\delta_0\), \(|\phi(\text{endpoint})|\le(1+\sqrt2)\) times its mean absolute value (the extreme case \(\phi(t)=t-c\), \(c=\delta_0(1-1/\sqrt2)\)), so \(|F_e|\le3\delta_0^{-1}\int_Q|\Phi^1|\), \(Q\) the cell before \(e\). Young. With \(s=3L_0\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \(ab\le\frac{Ns}4(\psi_2(\frac{4a}{Ns})+\psi_2^*(b))\): \(|F_e||\Delta_eg|=\delta_0^2\frac{|F_e|}{\delta_0}\frac{|\Delta_eg|}{\delta_0}\le\frac{Ns}4\delta_0^2\big(\psi_2(\frac{12}{Ns}\operatorname{avg}_Q|\Phi|)+\psi_2^*(\frac{|\Delta_eg|}{\delta_0})\big)\), and \(\frac{12}{Ns}=\frac4{L_0\sqrt{N\log N}}\); by Jensen \(\delta_0^2\psi_2(\frac{12}{Ns}\operatorname{avg}_Q|\Phi|)\le\int_Q\psi_2(4|\Phi|/(L_0\sqrt{N\log N}))\). Each cell comes before at most one edge in each direction, so these terms sum to at most \(2I\le1\), and \(\frac{Ns}4=\frac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}\): this is (a). (b) Let \(v=|\Delta_eg|/\delta_0\le Y\). If \(v/2\ge e^{16}\): \(\psi_2^*(v)\le v\sqrt{\log(1+v)}\) (lem:flow-coarea-level-bound (b)) and \(\psi^*_\alpha(v/2)\ge\frac{v/2}{2\sqrt2}(\log(v/2))^{1/\alpha}\) (same, for \(\alpha=\infty\) with exponent \(0\)); with \(\log(1+v)\le1.06\log(v/2)\), \(\psi_2^*(v)\le5.9(\log Y)^{1/2-1/\alpha}\psi^*_\alpha(v/2)\). If \(v/2<e^{16}\): \(\psi_2^*(v)\le0.021+v\sqrt{\log(1+2e^{16})}\le0.021+4.1v\) and \(v\le2\psi^*_\alpha(v/2)+2(e-1)\), so \(\psi_2^*(v)\le8.2\psi^*_\alpha(v/2)+14.2\). Summing over edges with \(\sum_e\delta_0^2\le2\) and the cost at most \(2\): \(\sum_e\delta_0^2\psi_2^*(v)\le11.8\max_j(\log\max\{Y,2e^{16}\})^{1/2-1/\alpha_j}+16.4+28.4\), and (a) gives (b). (c) At \((4,4)\) the exponent is \(\frac14\), giving \(C(1+(\log Y)^{1/4})\); lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) with \(\kappa=4\) gives \(8L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}(\log(y/2))^{-1/4}\) on its event; both hold on the intersection. For the chain, \(\Delta_e\sum_k1_{A_k}\) counts, with one sign (the sets being nested), the boundaries \(\partial A_k\) through \(e\), at most \(m\) of them; so every increment is \(ky\delta_0\) with \(0\le k\le m\), the nonzero ones in \([y\delta_0,my\delta_0]\), and (b) applies with \(Y=my\). Without the bound \(m\) nesting does not limit the increments: a cell in every \(A_k\) beside one in none has increment \(Ky\delta_0\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Dyadic \(\delta_0\): the flow's squares nest down to the cells and their midlines are grid lines. \(\delta_0\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\): the Chernoff event \(E_1\) at level \(J\). One sequence \(\delta_0(N)\): the flow's event is shown for a fixed level \(J(N)\), through a Chebyshev step without a rate, so no union over \(\delta_0\) is made. \(L_0\): the event \(I\le\frac12\). The cost and \(Y\): only in (b). \(\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\) and \(y\ge2e^{16}\): only the second bound in (c), through lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c). Independence: the points i.i.d. uniform, through the flow's martingale tail and the fine-grid lemma. Conclusions: (a) for every grid function; (b) for the discrete class at every pair in \([2,\infty]^2\) with increments at most \(Y\delta_0\); (c) at \((4,4)\) for increments between \(y\delta_0\) and \(Y\delta_0\), and nested chains at level \(y\) with at most \(m\) boundaries through each edge (the bound \(m\) is used to cap the increments at \(my\delta_0\); the chain clause uses only (b), so it needs neither \(\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\) nor \(y\ge2e^{16}\)); all for the \(X\)-term.

Baseline. The plainest recorded bound for the discrete class is lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) and (c), \(\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}(g)\), which at level \((\log N)^2\) is \(\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}(2\log\log N)^{-1/4}\) up to constants, above the target by about \((\log N/\log\log N)^{1/4}\); the record's continuous flow bound, lem:flow-coarea-level-bound, needs Lipschitz functions. What the lemma adds: the dyadic flow's fluxes across cell edges, through its affine structure on the cells, bound every grid function, so the discrete class is bounded at every pair up to \((\log Y)^{1/2-1/\alpha}\); at polylogarithmic levels this beats the fine-grid bound by \((\log N)^{1/4}\) up to powers of \(\log\log N\).

Degenerate cases. \(g\) constant: \(D(g)=g\sum_Q(n_Q-N\delta_0^2)=0\), and all increments vanish. One cell raised: four edges carry the cost, and (a) gives the order \(\sqrt{N\log N}(1+4\delta_0^2\psi_2^*(|g_Q|/\delta_0))\), against the plain count \(|g_Q||n_Q-N\delta_0^2|\). \(Y<2e^{16}\): (b) is stated with \(\max\{Y,2e^{16}\}\) and gives the conjectured order. \(\delta_0\) at its lower end \(4\sqrt{\log N/N}\): \(N\delta_0^2=16\log N\), the flow's event still holds.

Nonvacuity. On the curve's parameters at \((4,4)\), for (c)'s chain clause at the review's level and multiplicity: \(\delta_0\) the dyadic number in \([4\sqrt{\log N/N},8\sqrt{\log N/N})\), at most \(2^{-\ell_1}\) for large \(N\); \(y=(\log N)^2\ge2e^{16}\) once \(\log N\ge e^{8.4}\); \(A_1\) a square block of cells of side \(b\) with its lower left corner at \((\frac14,\frac14)\), \(b\) the largest multiple of \(2\delta_0\) with \(b\le\frac12\) and \(5b\delta_0\psi_4^*(y)\le2\), so \(A_1\) stays away from \(\partial[0,1]^2\) and all its boundary edges are inner edges, and \(A_2\subseteq A_1\) the block of side \(b/2\) in its lower left corner, so \(K=2\), the \(b/\delta_0\) edges along the shared halves of two sides lie on both boundaries (\(m=2\)) and carry the increment \(2y\delta_0\), and the other \(4b/\delta_0\) boundary edges of the two blocks carry \(y\delta_0\). The cost is \(b\delta_0(\psi_4^*(y)+4\psi_4^*(y/2))\le5b\delta_0\psi_4^*(y)\le2\), and \(b\ge2\delta_0\) because \(\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(y)\le64(\log N)^3(\log(1+y))^{1/4}/N\to0\). For this one \(g\), \(D(g)=y\delta_0\sum_{k=1,2}(n_{A_k}-N\lambda(A_k))\), each a centred binomial count of standard deviation at most \(\sqrt{N}b\); with \(\psi_4^*(y)\ge\frac y{2\sqrt2}(\log y)^{1/4}\) (the recorded lower bound, as in lem:flow-coarea-level-bound) the cost gives \(y\delta_0b\le\frac{4\sqrt2}5(\log y)^{-1/4}\), so \(O(\sqrt N)\), and a union over the at most \(N^2\) such pairs of blocks adds \(\sqrt{\log N}\); the lemma's content is the uniformity over all grid functions of this level and multiplicity, where lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor gives \(\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}(\log(y/2))^{-1/4}\).

Smeared Y-term is O(√N) across the class

17 October 2026 · Working proof; evenly spread Y · Smearing terms. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: An equivalent form of the goal's open statement up to O(sqrt N); the goal's state in Where we stand is unchanged.

Question. The discrete flow bound named as next attempt the fifth review's gap-charged bound for nested chains, first on two nested blocks; it and every recent entry left the \(Y\)-term of the smeared discrepancy aside, and the record names the conversion between the Lebesgue and the smeared forms as open (lem:dominant-level-split's Not covered, the fourth review). The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy; this entry first tries the named smallest case with the plainest bound, then asks what the smeared \(Y\)-term and the smearing of the \(X\)-term cost for every class function.

Target form. The goal's form is the class bound for the cell-smeared \(\mu_X-\mu_Y\) on the reduction's grid; this entry works in that form itself, on every square grid with \(1/\delta\) an integer (part (b) with side at least \(20/\sqrt N\)), and adds nothing to it.

Chosen. The chaining lead entry-2026-10-16-fourth-route-review:2, not the queue head sandpile-odometer-flow: its latest follow-up named the attempt this entry tries first, and it bears directly on conjugate-class-discrepancy.

General statement. lem:smeared-y-term: part (a) for every evenly spread \(Y\), every square grid with \(1/\delta\) an integer and every function in \(W^{1,1}\); part (b) for such grids with \(\delta\ge20/\sqrt N\) and every exponent pair in \([1,\infty]^2\); part (c) for every grid of side \(\delta\ge\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\); part (d) at \((4,4)\) on the reduction's grid.

The named smallest case

Smallest case tried. Two nested square blocks of cells \(A_1\supseteq A_2\) of sides \(b_1,b_2\) on a grid of side \(\delta_0\ge\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\), at level \(y\): \(g=y\delta_0(1_{A_1}+1_{A_2})\). The blocks of cells number at most \(\delta_0^{-4}\le N^2\); Bernstein's inequality for each block's count with \(t=4\log N\) and a union over them give, with probability at least \(1-2N^{-2}\), \(|n_A-N\lambda(A)|\le\sqrt{8N\lambda(A)\log N}+4\log N\) for every block \(A\). So \(|D(g)|\le y\delta_0\big(\sqrt{8N\log N}(b_1+b_2)+8\log N\big)\). The cost is at least \(\frac{4(b_1+b_2)}{\delta_0}\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(y/2)\) (an edge on both boundaries carries \(\psi_4^*(y)\ge2\psi_4^*(y/2)\), by convexity and \(\psi_4^*(0)=0\)), and \(\psi_4^*(y/2)\ge\frac y{4\sqrt2}(\log(y/2))^{1/4}\), so cost at most \(2\) gives \(y\delta_0(b_1+b_2)\le2\sqrt2(\log(y/2))^{-1/4}\) and \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}(\log(y/2))^{-1/4}+8y\delta_0\log N\); since \(b_k\ge\delta_0\), the cost also gives \(\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(y/2)\le\frac12\), so \(y\delta_0^2\le2\sqrt2\) and \(8y\delta_0\log N\le8(2\sqrt2y)^{1/2}\log N=o(\sqrt{N\log N})\) for \(y\le N^{1-\epsilon}\). This is the operation's predicted order: the named smallest case is decided by the plainest bound, and the discrete flow bound's Smallest case, which named lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) as the plainest uniform bound for such pairs, was wrong there; the operation's content lies in families too large for a union bound, layers whose boundaries take exponentially many shapes.

Smeared terms

Setting. \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\); \(Y_1,\dots,Y_N\) evenly spread: rectangles \(R_j\) of area \(1/N\) with disjoint interiors covering the square, \(Y_j\in R_j\subset B(Y_j,10/\sqrt N)\). A grid of square cells \(Q\) of side \(\delta\), \(1/\delta\) an integer; \(Q(z)\) the cell of \(z\); \(\mu_X=\sum_i\mathrm{Unif}(Q(X_i))\), \(\mu_Y=\sum_j\mathrm{Unif}(Q(Y_j))\); \(E_QG\) the average of \(G\) on \(Q\), \(\|\nabla G\|_1=\int(|\partial_1G|+|\partial_2G|)\), \(\Lambda_\delta(G)=\sum_Q\mathrm{Lip}(G|_Q)\lambda(Q)\).

Statement. (a) Every \(G\in W^{1,1}\) (in particular every Lipschitz \(G\)) has \(\big|\int G\,d\mu_Y-N\int G\big|\le40\sqrt N\big(1+\frac{20}{\delta\sqrt N}\big)\|\nabla G\|_1\), at most \(80\sqrt N\,\|\nabla G\|_1\) when \(\delta\ge20/\sqrt N\). (b) Hence, for every pair \(\alpha\in[1,\infty]^2\) and every \(G\) with \(\int\sum_j\psi^*_{\alpha_j}(|\partial_jG|)\le2\), \(\|\nabla G\|_1\le2e\) and the \(Y\)-term is at most \(160e\sqrt N\); so the class discrepancy \(D_N=\sup_G\int G\,d(\mu_X-\mu_Y)\) and the class supremum \(D^X_N\) of the \(X\)-term \(\sum_i(E_{Q(X_i)}G)-N\int G\) satisfy \(|D_N-D^X_N|\le160e\sqrt N\). (c) If \(\delta\ge\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(\kappa>0\) fixed, then with probability tending to one every cell holds at most \(c_\kappa N\delta^2\) points of \(X\), \(c_\kappa=\max(e^2,2/\kappa^2)\), simultaneously for one grid sequence and for all dyadic \(\delta\) in that range, and on that event every \(G\) Lipschitz on each cell has \(\big|\sum_i(E_{Q(X_i)}G-G(X_i))\big|\le\sqrt2\,c_\kappa N\delta\,\Lambda_\delta(G)\). (d) At \((4,4)\), on the reduction's grid (\(\delta=1/\lceil32/s\rceil\), \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(L\ge132\)), with probability tending to one, every class function whose larger partial is at least \(y\ge e^{16}\) where \(\nabla G\ne0\) has \(\int G\,d(\mu_X-\mu_Y)\le C_L\sqrt{N\log N}(1+\Lambda_j(G))\) for every \(j\) with \(1\le j\le j^*(y)\), \(j^*(y)\) and \(\Lambda_j\) as in lem:dominant-level-split.

Proof. (a) Since \(N\lambda(R_j)=1\), \(N\int G=\sum_Q N\lambda(Q)E_QG\) and \(\int G\,d\mu_Y=\sum_Qn^Y_QE_QG\), \(n^Y_Q=\#\{j:Y_j\in Q\}\). Move, for each \(j\) and each \(x\in R_j\), the density \(N\) at \(x\) from \(Q(x)\) to \(Q(Y_j)\), \(|x-Y_j|\le10/\sqrt N\); route a move first along the row of \(x\) to the column of \(Y_j\), then along that column (when \(\delta\ge20/\sqrt N\) the two cells are equal or neighbours, but the bound below does not need it). Let \(F_e\) be the net mass carried across the inner edge \(e\) from its cell \(Q\) to the next cell \(Q'\). The mass ending in \(Q\) is \(n^Y_Q\) and the mass starting there \(N\lambda(Q)\), so \(n^Y_Q-N\lambda(Q)\) is the net inflow, and summing by parts \(\int G\,d\mu_Y-N\int G=\sum_QE_QG\,(n^Y_Q-N\lambda(Q))=\sum_eF_e(E_{Q'}G-E_QG)\). A vertical edge at \(x_1=t\) carries only row moves, from points of its row (a strip of height \(\delta\)) within \(10/\sqrt N\) of the line \(x_1=t\): \(|F_e|\le N\cdot\delta\cdot20/\sqrt N=20\delta\sqrt N\). A horizontal edge at \(x_2=t\) in column \(c\) carries only column moves, of mass that started at points within \(10/\sqrt N\) of the line \(x_2=t\) and within \(10/\sqrt N\) of column \(c\) (since \(Y_j\) lies in it): \(|F_e|\le N(\delta+20/\sqrt N)\cdot20/\sqrt N=20\sqrt N(\delta+20/\sqrt N)\), which also bounds the vertical edges' \(20\delta\sqrt N\). The translation sweep: for cells side by side in direction \(e_k\), \(E_{Q'}G-E_QG=\delta^{-2}\int_Q\int_0^\delta\partial_kG(z+re_k)\,dr\,dz\) (for \(G\in W^{1,1}\), absolutely continuous on almost every line), so \(\delta|E_{Q'}G-E_QG|\le\int_{Q\cup Q'}|\partial_kG|\), and each cell lies in at most two pairs per direction: \(\sum_e\delta|E_{Q'}G-E_QG|\le2\|\nabla G\|_1\). Hence the bound \(20\sqrt N(\delta+20/\sqrt N)\cdot2\|\nabla G\|_1/\delta\). (b) For finite \(\alpha\ge1\), \(\psi^*_\alpha(t)\ge t\cdot1-\psi_\alpha(1)=t-(e-1)\), and \(\psi^*_\infty(t)=t\) for \(t\le N\) and \(+\infty\) beyond; so \(\int|\partial_jG|\le\int\psi^*_{\alpha_j}(|\partial_jG|)+e-1\) and \(\|\nabla G\|_1\le2+2(e-1)=2e\). Then \(\int G\,d(\mu_X-\mu_Y)\) is the \(X\)-term minus the \(Y\)-term, the latter at most \(160e\sqrt N\) in absolute value for every class function, which gives both inequalities between the suprema. (c) \(n_Q\) is binomial with mean \(m=N\delta^2\ge\kappa^2\log N\); for \(c\ge e^2\), \(\Pr(n_Q\ge cm)\le(e/c)^{cm}\le e^{-cm}\le N^{-c\kappa^2}\le N^{-2}\) when also \(c\ge2/\kappa^2\); one grid has at most \(N/(\kappa^2\log N)\) cells and all dyadic grids in the range at most \(2N/(\kappa^2\log N)\), so the union tends to zero. On that event, \(|E_QG-G(X_i)|\le\mathrm{osc}_Q(G)\le\sqrt2\,\delta\,\mathrm{Lip}(G|_Q)\) for \(X_i\in Q\) (a cell is convex of diameter \(\sqrt2\delta\)), and summing over the at most \(c_\kappa N\delta^2\) points of each cell gives \(\sqrt2c_\kappa N\delta^3\sum_Q\mathrm{Lip}(G|_Q)=\sqrt2c_\kappa N\delta\Lambda_\delta(G)\). (d) lem:dominant-level-split gives \(|\sum_iG(X_i)-N\int G|\le L'\sqrt{N\log N}(1+\Lambda_j(G))\) on its event; (c) with \(\kappa=L/33\) (\(\delta\ge s/33\) for large \(N\)) adds \(\sqrt2e^2N\delta\Lambda_\delta(G)\) with \(N\delta\le Ns/32=\frac L{32}\sqrt{N\log N}\); and \(\Lambda_\delta(G)\le4\Lambda_j(G)\) for large \(N\): \(G\) is Lipschitz, so on a cell \(Q\) of the grid its Lipschitz constant is at most the largest over the dyadic cells \(D\) of side \(2^{-j}\) meeting \(Q\), and \(\sum_Q\lambda(Q)\max_{D\cap Q\ne\emptyset}\mathrm{Lip}(G|_D)\le\sum_D\mathrm{Lip}(G|_D)(2^{-j}+2\delta)^2=(1+2\delta2^j)^2\Lambda_j(G)\), where \(j\le j^*(y)\le\ell_1\) gives \(2^{-j}\ge(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\) and so \(\delta2^j\le\frac L{32}(\log N)^{-1/4}\to0\). With (b)'s \(Y\)-term, \(\int G\,d(\mu_X-\mu_Y)\le L'(1+\Lambda_j(G))\sqrt{N\log N}+\frac{\sqrt2e^2L}{32}(1+2\delta2^j)^2\Lambda_j(G)\sqrt{N\log N}+160e\sqrt N\), the middle coefficient tending to \(\frac{\sqrt2e^2}{32}L\approx0.33L\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Evenly spread \(Y\): (a)'s moves, each within \(10/\sqrt N\), and \(N\lambda(R_j)=1\). \(\delta\ge20/\sqrt N\): only to simplify (a)'s constant to \(80\); the flux bound holds for every \(\delta\). \(1/\delta\) an integer: the cells tile the square, so the outer edges carry nothing. \(G\in W^{1,1}\): the sweep (absolute continuity on almost every line, Fubini) in (a); in (c), Lipschitz on each cell suffices. The class cost: only (b) and (d), through \(\psi^*_\alpha(t)\ge t-(e-1)\). \(\delta\ge\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and independence of the \(X_i\): the Chernoff bound for the cell counts in (c). The level \(y\ge e^{16}\) and \(1\le j\le j^*(y)\): (d), through lem:dominant-level-split, and \(j\le\ell_1\) for the comparison of \(\Lambda_\delta\) with \(\Lambda_j\). Conclusions: (a) deterministic, for every function in \(W^{1,1}\), every grid and every evenly spread configuration; (b) for every class function at every pair in \([1,\infty]^2\); (c) for every function Lipschitz on each cell, with probability tending to one; (d) at \((4,4)\) for the single-level class functions, on the reduction's grid, with probability tending to one.

Baseline. The plainest recorded bound of the \(Y\)-side is the one in the proof of lem:lipschitz-class-lower-bound: \(O(\sqrt N)\) for \(1\)-Lipschitz functions, from \(|E_QG-G(Y_j)|\le10/\sqrt N+\sqrt2\delta\) over the at most \(80(1/\delta+1)\sqrt N\) rectangles meeting a grid line; for class functions, whose gradients are unbounded, the oscillation of \(G\) near a rectangle is not bounded, and the plain count gives nothing. What the lemma adds: (a) bounds the \(Y\)-term of every function in \(W^{1,1}\) by its gradient mass, through a flow of edge fluxes \(O(\delta\sqrt N+1)\), so the class's \(Y\)-term is \(O(\sqrt N)\) at every pair and the goal's smeared discrepancy is its \(X\)-term up to \(O(\sqrt N)\); (c) is a bare per-cell count, whose use is (d): the record's Lebesgue bound for single-level functions carried to the goal's form.

Degenerate cases. \(G\) constant: both sides of (a) and (c) vanish. One cell (\(\delta=1\)): \(\mu_Y=N\lambda\), the \(Y\)-term is zero, and (a) holds. \(Y\) the centres of a square grid of side \(1/\sqrt N\) aligned with cells whose side is a multiple of it: \(n^Y_Q=N\lambda(Q)\) and the \(Y\)-term is zero. \(\delta<20/\sqrt N\): a move may cross several cells, and (a) holds with the factor \(1+20/(\delta\sqrt N)\). A function that is constant on the cells: \(\Lambda_\delta=0\) and (c) is an equality, \(E_QG=G\); (c) says nothing about cell functions, which (a) and (b) do not need.

Nonvacuity. On the curve's parameters at \((4,4)\), for (d): the witness of lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound, which lem:dominant-level-split records as satisfying its hypotheses with \(\Lambda_{\ell_1}\le297/L\), on the reduction's grid, where \(\delta\le s/32\le2^{-\ell_1}\) for large \(N\); (d) gives \(\int G\,d(\mu_X-\mu_Y)\le C_L(1+297/L)\sqrt{N\log N}\), and lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound gives \(D_N\ge\sqrt{N\log N}/(4L_1)\) on the curve, so the class supremum \(D_N\) is of that order (that lemma bounds the supremum, not this witness's own discrepancy). For (a): \(N\) a perfect square and any evenly spread \(Y\) not aligned with the grid, such as the centres of the \(1/\sqrt N\) grid shifted by \((\frac1{3\sqrt N},0)\) (the rectangles shifted with them and cut at the boundary), with \(\delta=1/\lfloor\sqrt N/20\rfloor\), and \(G(x)=x_1\), \(\|\nabla G\|_1=1\). Plainest bound. For one fixed \(G\) the \(Y\)-term is deterministic and the proof of lem:lipschitz-class-lower-bound bounds it when \(G\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz; for \(G=x_1\) it gives \(O(\sqrt N)\) as (a) does; the lemma's content is the class, gradients unbounded, uniformly.

Architecture test

Architecture test. Not decided. The fifth review's operation, the gap-charged bound for nested chains, was not proved or refuted; its named smallest case, two nested blocks, is decided at the operation's order by a union bound over the at most \(N^2\) blocks; on the reviewer's decomposition, a nested pair being its inner layer plus a band, and its unverified heuristic that the pair is never better than its inner layer, the operation's content is the single layer whose perimeter spends the budget, with boundaries of exponentially many shapes. By (b), each \(X\)-term bound the operation would give is a bound of the goal's smeared form up to \(160e\sqrt N\).

For the next attempt as first drafted, "gap charged nested chains local gap two nested blocks boundaries layers tube" (the previous cycle) returned lem:tube-localized-discrepancy and lem:band-family-discrepancy, whose part (a) covers column-interval sets; for the attempt as retargeted, "union of cells perimeter closed lattice curve single layer cut cells variance Bernstein isoperimetric" returned lem:tube-localized-discrepancy, lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor, lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy and lem:loglog-mesh-deviation, each stated on meshes of at least the Leighton–Shor scale except the fine-grid lemma, which charges cut cells the full factor. tools/claim_resemblance.py on the spec: lem:flow-coarea-level-bound and conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy (0.50), cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction (0.41), lem:dominant-level-split (0.40) and lem:lipschitz-class-lower-bound (0.37), each related in the spec; none is a more general version.

Goal progress. Unchanged: no implication toward conj:ultimate-matching changed; (b) is an equivalent form of conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy up to \(O(\sqrt N)\), not progress toward it. Bearing. Follow-up

Item history. The item's earlier entries, read in this cycle or the previous one: the discrete flow bound, whose follow-up named "the fifth review's operation, the gap-charged bound for nested chains with at most two boundaries through each edge"; the fine-grid entry: "the curve-trace attempt in the discrete class, a band-confined layer bound"; the sample-point pyramids entry, which "still bears on conjugate-class-discrepancy, now through the discrete class of the Smeared form paragraph"; the band-family entry, where "the reviewer found that the closure does not stand, since the decisive split's tube part" is made of level curves; and the tube-localized entry: "The item still bears on conjugate-class-discrepancy through plateau bands with ramps between" two scales.

Owed attempt. The operation named by the discrete flow bound was made on its named smallest case only, two nested blocks, which the plainest bound decides (above); the operation itself was not made, and the smearing terms came first because every bound it would give is for the \(X\)-term, which (b) turns into a bound of the goal's form.

Follow-up. Continuing. The item's translation, chaining against the class, still bears on conjugate-class-discrepancy at polylogarithmic levels and near \(e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\), now in the \(X\)-term alone. The reviewer's decomposition retargets the operation: \(1_{A_1}+1_{A_2}=2\cdot1_{A_2}+1_{A_1\setminus A_2}\) (the identity checked here), so a nested pair at level \(y\) is its inner layer at level \(2y\) plus a band of width \(\sigma\) along \(\partial A_1\); that the pair's supremum is then never better than its inner layer's, up to the band, is the reviewer's heuristic, unverified, and on it the operation's content is the single layer at level \(y\) whose perimeter \(P\) spends the budget, \(P\approx2/(\delta_0\psi_4^*(y/2))\). Next attempt: for a union \(A\) of cells of side \(\delta_0\) with perimeter \(P\ge1\), \(|D(A)|\le C\sqrt N\,P\big((2\log_2\max(1,2^{\ell_1}/P)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\big)\), by the fine-grid split: the coarse averages at the Leighton–Shor mesh, a cell function with values in \([0,1]\), charged by lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (b) with tube width \(W=\max(1/P,2^{-\ell_1})\) (its extra term \(4W\sum(\max H^++\max H^-)\) is at most \(8WP^2=8P\) when \(W=1/P\), and at most \(8\cdot2^{\ell_1}<8P\) when \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\)), and the cut coarse cells charged by Bernstein's inequality with the variance \(n_Cp(1-p)\) instead of the count, with \(p(1-p)\) bounded through the isoperimetric inequality inside the coarse cell by the boundary length there; the cost \(P\delta_0\psi_4^*(y/2)\le2\) with \(\psi_4^*(y/2)\ge\frac y{4\sqrt2}(\log(y/2))^{1/4}\) gives \(P\le P_{\mathrm{sat}}=8\sqrt2/(y\delta_0(\log(y/2))^{1/4})\), so \(y\delta_0P\le8\sqrt2(\log(y/2))^{-1/4}\). The bound \(P\big((2\log_2\max(1,2^{\ell_1}/P)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\big)\) increases in \(P\) (with \(b=2\log_2(c/P)+5\), the derivative of \(Pb^{3/4}\) is \(b^{-1/4}(b-\frac3{2\ln2})\), positive as \(b\ge5\)), so for \(g=y\delta_01_A\) it is largest at \(P_{\mathrm{sat}}\), where \(2^{\ell_1}/P_{\mathrm{sat}}\le y(\log y)^{1/4}\) since \(\delta_02^{\ell_1}\le1\); the coarse factor is then at most \((2\log_2(y(\log y)^{1/4})+5)^{3/4}\), and the bound for \(g\) is \(C\sqrt N(\log y)^{1/2}+C\sqrt{N\log N}(\log y)^{-1/4}\), of the conjectured order for every \(y\le N\). A layer with \(P<1\) is bounded by lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) directly, \(|D(A)|\le L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}P\) with no additive term, so \(g\) is at most \(L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\min\{y\delta_0,\,8\sqrt2(\log(y/2))^{-1/4}\}\): at most of order \(\sqrt{N\log N}\) when \(y\delta_0\le(\log N)^{-1/4}\), and \(o(\sqrt{N\log N})\) at polylogarithmic \(y\), where \(y\delta_0\to0\). Smallest case. \(A\) a union of \(M\) disjoint square blocks of cells of side \(\ell\ge\delta_0\), \(P=4M\ell\) the sum of the blocks' perimeters: on the event of the Smallest case tried above, each block deviates by at most \(\ell\sqrt{8N\log N}+4\log N\), so \(|D(A)|\le\frac P4\sqrt{8N\log N}+4M\log N\), and \(4M\log N=P\log N/\ell\le P\sqrt{N\log N}/\kappa\) as \(\ell\ge\delta_0\ge\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\): order \(\sqrt{N\log N}\,P\), the target's; so blocks are decided by the plainest bound, and the first case that tests the attempt is a union of pieces whose boundaries wiggle below the Leighton–Shor mesh. Own statements. Parts (a)–(d) bound the \(Y\)-term and Lipschitz functions; (c) is an equality on cell functions. lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (a), lem:loglog-mesh-deviation and lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (a) and (b) charge closed curves and cell functions on meshes of at least \(2^{-\ell_1}\) by the logarithm of their length in mesh units, the target's form, and (b) decides the coarse part of the attempt; on the grid of side \(\delta_0<2^{-\ell_1}\) they do not apply, and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) charges the cut cells \((\log N)^{3/4}\) per unit perimeter, so the record decides the coarse part and not the fine one. Plainest bound. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a), \(\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}P\).

Cut-cell variance bound below the mesh

17 October 2026 · Working proof; (b)–(d) on dyadic grids · Cut-cell variance. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: A subfamily of the discrete class bounded and the rest of the single-level class reduced to coarse averages; the goal's state in Where we stand is unchanged.

Question. The smeared terms entry reduced the goal's smeared form to the \(X\)-term and named as next attempt the single layer whose perimeter \(P\) spends the budget, charged \(C\sqrt N\,P\big((2\log_2\max(1,2^{\ell_1}/P)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\big)\): the coarse averages by tube localization, the cut coarse cells by Bernstein's inequality with the variance and isoperimetry inside each coarse cell. The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy; the record's bound for single layers at level \(y\), lem:discrete-flow-bound (c), loses \(\min\{(\log y)^{1/4},(\log N/\log(y/2))^{1/4}\}\), up to \((\log N)^{1/8}\) near \(y=e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\), and this entry makes the named attempt.

Target form. The goal's form is the class bound for the cell-smeared \(\mu_X-\mu_Y\) on the reduction's grid; this entry works in the discrete \(X\)-term \(D(g)=\sum_ig(X_i)-N\int g\) of grid functions against Lebesgue measure. By lem:smeared-y-term (b) the goal's smeared discrepancy of a class function \(G\) is the \(X\)-term of its cell averages up to \(160e\sqrt N\), so a bound here for a family of grid functions is a bound of the goal's form only for the class functions whose cell averages lie in that family; the cell averages of a continuous single-level function take every increment below the level (the Levels paragraph of the fine-grid entry), so they are not the chains of (c) in general. Part (a) holds on the reduction's own grid, of side \(1/\lceil32/s\rceil\), with every coarse grid it refines by a factor \(m\le\sqrt{\log N}\) dividing \(\lceil32/s\rceil\); when \(\lceil32/s\rceil\) has no divisor \(1<m\le\sqrt{\log N}\) (for instance, it is prime) the only such coarse grid is the grid itself and (a) says nothing there (coarse rectangles of \(m\) or \(m+1\) fine cells a side might serve, with an isoperimetric constant depending on the aspect ratio: the reviewer's suggestion, unverified); parts (b)–(d) need a dyadic grid, which the reduction's is not.

General statement. lem:cut-cell-variance-bound: part (a) for every pair of square grids of sides \(\delta_0\le W\), \(1/W\) and \(W/\delta_0\) integers, with \(\delta_0\ge\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \((W/\delta_0)^2\le\log N\), every grid function, every fixed \(\kappa>0\); part (b) for every union of cells with perimeter at least \(1\) on dyadic grids between \(\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \(2^{-\ell_1}\); parts (c) and (d) for every nested chain at \((4,4)\) on such grids, at every level \(y\ge2e^{16}\).

Cut-cell variance

Setting. \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\); \(\ell_1\) the Leighton–Shor scale, the largest integer with \(2^{-\ell_1}\ge(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\), so \(2^{-\ell_1}<2(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\); \(\kappa>0\) fixed. For a mesh \(\delta_0\) with \(1/\delta_0\) an integer (dyadic in (b)–(d)), \(g\) constant on its cells, \(D(g)=\sum_ig(X_i)-N\int g\), \(\mathrm{TV}(g)=\sum_e\delta_0|\Delta_eg|\) over the inner edges, \(P(A)=\mathrm{TV}(1_A)\) the inner perimeter of a union \(A\) of cells; for a grid of side \(W\ge\delta_0\) whose cells are unions of cells of side \(\delta_0\), \(E_Wg\) the averages of \(g\) on the cells of side \(W\), \(n_C\) the number of points in a cell \(C\). \(\psi_4^*\) is the conjugate of \(\psi_4(t)=e^{t^4}-1\); the discrete cost of \(g\) is \(\sum_e\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eg|/(2\delta_0))\). A nested chain at level \(y\) is \(g=y\delta_0\sum_{k\le K}1_{A_k}\) with \(A_1\supseteq\dots\supseteq A_K\) unions of cells (a layer that is empty or the whole square has \(P_k=0\) and \(D(1_{A_k})=0\), so it changes neither side); \(P_k=P(A_k)\).

Statement. Let \(c_\kappa=\sqrt{10+20/\kappa^2}+\frac5{3\kappa}\). With probability tending to one: (a) for all square grids of sides \(\delta_0\le W\) with \(1/W\) and \(W/\delta_0\) integers, \(\delta_0\ge\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \((W/\delta_0)^2\le\log N\) (dyadic or not), every \(g\) constant on the cells of side \(\delta_0\) has \(|D(g)-D(E_Wg)|\le c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,\mathrm{TV}(g)\); (b) for every dyadic \(\delta_0\) with \(\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\le\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\), every union \(A\) of its cells with \(P(A)\ge1\) has \(|D(1_A)|\le C_b\sqrt N\,P(A)\big((2\log_2\max(1,2^{\ell_1}/P(A))+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\big)\), \(C_b=13L+c_\kappa\), \(L\) the constant of lem:tube-localized-discrepancy; (c) at \((4,4)\), on such grids, every nested chain at level \(y\ge2e^{16}\) with discrete cost at most \(2\) has, with \(T=8(\log(y/2))^{-1/4}\) and \(L_f\) the constant of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor, \[|D(g)|\le C_b\sqrt N\,T\big((2\log_2(Ky^2)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\big)+L_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\,y\delta_0\!\!\sum_{k:P_k<1}\!\!P_k;\] (d) hence, for \(N\) large, \(|D(g)|\le C_d\sqrt{N\log N}\), \(C_d=\max(55C_b+1,8\sqrt3L_f)\), for every such chain with \(K\le N^{1/7}\) and \(\log K\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y/2))^{1/3}\); in particular for every single layer (\(K=1\)) at every level \(y\ge2e^{16}\).

Relative isoperimetry. Let \(C\) be a square of side \(W\) cut into \(m\times m\) cells, \(B\) a union of some of them, and \(\ell\) the length of the cell edges inside \(C\) separating \(B\) from \(C\setminus B\). Then \(\min(\lambda(B),\lambda(C\setminus B))\le\ell^2/2\). Proof: call a column of cells full, empty or mixed as it lies in \(B\), in \(C\setminus B\) or meets both; a mixed column holds two vertically adjacent cells on opposite sides, so a horizontal separating edge; with \(b\) and \(b'\) the total widths of the mixed columns and rows, \(\ell\ge b+b'\). If every column is mixed, or every row, then \(\ell\ge W\) and \(\min\le W^2/2\le\ell^2/2\). If there is no full column and no full row, every cell of \(B\) lies in a mixed column and a mixed row, so \(\lambda(B)\le bb'\le(b+b')^2/4\le\ell^2/4\); symmetrically, if there is no empty column and no empty row, \(\lambda(C\setminus B)\le\ell^2/4\). In every other case there is a full column or a full row, and an empty column or an empty row. A full column and an empty row share a cell, as do an empty column and a full row, so these pairs cannot occur; a full column and an empty column make every row mixed, and a full row and an empty row make every column mixed, the first case. \(\square\)

Proof. Events. (F1) Every cell \(C\) of every grid of side \(W=1/n'\ge\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\) has \(n_C\le2\mu_C+4\log N\), \(\mu_C=NW^2\): by Bernstein's inequality for the binomial count, \(n_C\le\mu_C+\sqrt{8\mu_C\log N}+\frac43\log N\) except with probability \(N^{-4}\), and \(\sqrt{8\mu_C\log N}\le\mu_C+2\log N\); there are at most \(\sum_{n'\le\sqrt N}n'^2\le N^{3/2}\) such cells. (F2) For each pair \(\delta_0\le W\) of (a) (\(1/\delta_0\le\sqrt N\) and \(W/\delta_0\le\sqrt{\log N}\), so at most \(N\) pairs for \(N\) large), conditionally on the counts of the cells of side \(W\) the points of distinct cells are independent and uniform in their cells; for each such cell \(C\) and each union \(B\) of the \(q=(W/\delta_0)^2\le\log N\) fine cells of \(C\), \(p=\lambda(B)/\lambda(C)\), the count \(\#(X\cap B)\) is binomial \((n_C,p)\), and Bernstein's inequality gives \(|\#(X\cap B)-n_Cp|\le\sqrt{2vt}+t/3\), \(v=n_Cp(1-p)\), except with probability \(2e^{-t}\); take \(t=q\log2+4\log N\le5\log N\), so the union over the \(2^q\) sets, the at most \(N\) cells and the pairs fails with probability at most \(2N^{-2}\). (F3) The event of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, used through lem:tube-localized-discrepancy, and the event of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor. (a) First \(g=1_A\). With \(p_C=\lambda(A\cap C)/\lambda(C)\), \(D(1_A)-D(E_W1_A)=\sum_C\big(\#(X\cap A\cap C)-N\lambda(A\cap C)-p_C(n_C-N\lambda(C))\big)=\sum_C(\#(X\cap A\cap C)-n_Cp_C)\), and a term vanishes unless \(0<p_C<1\). For such a cut cell let \(\ell_C\ge\delta_0\) be the length of the edges of \(\partial A\) inside \(C\); these are disjoint for distinct cells, so \(\sum_C\ell_C\le P(A)\) and there are at most \(P(A)/\delta_0\) cut cells. By relative isoperimetry \(p(1-p)\le\min(p,1-p)\le\ell_C^2/(2W^2)\), and on (F1) \(v\le(2NW^2+4\log N)\ell_C^2/(2W^2)\le N\ell_C^2(1+2/\kappa^2)\), as \(W^2\ge\kappa^2\log N/N\). On (F2) the cut cell contributes at most \(\ell_C\sqrt{10(1+2/\kappa^2)N\log N}+\frac53\log N\); summing, \(|D(1_A)-D(E_W1_A)|\le\sqrt{10+20/\kappa^2}\sqrt{N\log N}\,P(A)+\frac53\log N\,P(A)/\delta_0\le c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,P(A)\), as \(\delta_0\ge\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\). For general \(g\): \(F(g)=D(g)-D(E_Wg)\) is linear and vanishes on constants; with \(c=\min g\), \(g-c=\int_0^\infty1_{\{g-c>t\}}dt\), each set a union of cells, and \(\int_0^\infty P(\{g-c>t\})\,dt=\mathrm{TV}(g)\) (the layer cake of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b)); the union bound in (F2) covers every set at once, so (a) follows under the integral. (b) For \(N\) large, \((2^{-\ell_1}/\delta_0)^2\le4\sqrt{\log N}/\kappa^2\le\log N\), so (a) applies with \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\): \(|D(1_A)-D(H)|\le c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,P\), \(H=E_{2^{-\ell_1}}1_A\), \(P=P(A)\). For \(H\), lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (b) with \(j=\ell_1\) and \(k=\min(\ell_1,\lceil\log_2P\rceil)\ge0\): \(V^0_{\ell_1}(H)\le P+4\le5P\), the inner part at most \(P\) by the global Fubini count of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor's proof and the boundary ring at most \(4\) as \(0\le H\le1\); as \(H\ge0\), \(4W\sum_Q(\max_QH^++\max_QH^-)\le4W\cdot W^{-2}=4/W\), which is less than \(8P\) when \(P\le2^{\ell_1}\) (then \(W>1/(2P)\)) and equals \(4\cdot2^{\ell_1}<4P\) otherwise; and \(\ell_1-k\le\log_2\max(1,2^{\ell_1}/P)\). So \(|D(H)|\le13L\sqrt N\,P\,\Phi\), \(\Phi=(2\log_2\max(1,2^{\ell_1}/P)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\ge\sqrt{\log N}\), and (b) follows. (c) Nesting: across an edge between cells in \(h(u)\) and \(h(v)\) of the sets, \(|\Delta g|/\delta_0=y|h(u)-h(v)|\in\{0\}\cup[y,\infty)\), and the increments of the \(1_{A_k}\) across an edge have one sign, so \(\mathrm{TV}(g)=y\delta_0\sum_kP_k\); by lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c), \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T\), so \(\sum_kP_k\le P_{\max}=T/(y\delta_0)\). By linearity \(D(g)=y\delta_0\sum_kD(1_{A_k})\). Layers with \(P_k<1\): lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a), the second term. Layers with \(P_k\ge1\), \(K'\le K\) of them with \(S=\sum P_k\le P_{\max}\): let \(m=2^{-\ell_1}/\delta_0\), \(c=4m2^{\ell_1}=4/\delta_0\), \(u(P)=2\log_2(c/P)+5\). Every inner perimeter is below \(2/\delta_0=c/2\), so \(u(P_k)\ge7\) and \(u(P_k)\ge2\log_2\max(1,2^{\ell_1}/P_k)+5\); \(f(P)=Pu(P)^{3/4}\) has \(f'=u^{-1/4}(u-\frac3{2\ln2})>0\) and \(f''=-\frac2{P\ln2}\big(\frac34u^{-1/4}+\frac3{8\ln2}u^{-5/4}\big)<0\) on \((0,c/2]\). By (b) and Jensen's inequality, \(\sum_{P_k\ge1}|D(1_{A_k})|\le C_b\sqrt N\big(K'f(S/K')+S\sqrt{\log N}\big)\), and \(K'f(S/K')=Su(S/K')^{3/4}\le Su(S/K)^{3/4}\le P_{\max}u(P_{\max}/K)^{3/4}\), the function \(S\mapsto Su(S/K)^{3/4}\) having derivative \(f'(S/K)>0\); here \(P_{\max}\le4/(2e^{16}\delta_0)<c/2\) since \(T\le4\). Finally \(cK/P_{\max}=4Ky/T\le Ky^2\) (\(m2^{\ell_1}\delta_0=1\)), so \(u(P_{\max}/K)\le2\log_2(Ky^2)+5\), and multiplying by \(y\delta_0\), \(y\delta_0P_{\max}=T\) gives the first term. (d) For \(y\ge N^{1/3}\), lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) with \(c=1/3\) gives \(8\sqrt3L_f\sqrt{N\log N}\). For \(y<N^{1/3}\): with \(a=2\log_2K\le2.89\log K\) and \(b=4\log_2y+5\le6.4\log(y/2)\) (as \(\log(y/2)\ge16\)), \((a+b)^{3/4}\le a^{3/4}+b^{3/4}\), \(Ta^{3/4}\le8\cdot2.22(\log K)^{3/4}(\log(y/2))^{-1/4}\le17.8\sqrt{\log N}\) under the condition on \(K\), \(Tb^{3/4}\le8\cdot4.03(\log(y/2))^{1/2}\le32.3\sqrt{\log N}\), and \(T\sqrt{\log N}\le4\sqrt{\log N}\): the first term is at most \(55C_b\sqrt{N\log N}\) (\(17.8+32.3+4\le55\)). The second is at most \(L_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}Ky\delta_0\le2L_fK(\log N)^{3/2}N^{1/3}\), as \(y\delta_0<N^{1/3}2^{-\ell_1}\), which is \(o(\sqrt{N\log N})\) for \(K\le N^{1/7}\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Independence and uniformity of the points: the binomial counts in (F1) and their conditional law given the coarse counts in (F2), and the events of the cited lemmas. \(\delta_0\ge\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\), any fixed \(\kappa>0\): the variance bound's \(\log N/W^2\le N/\kappa^2\) and the conversion of \(P/\delta_0\) cut cells into \(\frac1\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,P\); the constants depend on \(\kappa\). \((W/\delta_0)^2\le\log N\): the union over the \(2^q\) subsets of a coarse cell with \(t\le5\log N\); a larger ratio puts \(t\approx q\log2\), and the two Bernstein terms then cost about \(\sqrt{Nq}+q\sqrt N/(\kappa\sqrt{\log N})\) per unit of variation instead of \(c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\), more as soon as \(q>\log N\). \(1/W\) and \(W/\delta_0\) integers: the fine cells nest in the coarse ones and the coarse cells tile the square, which is all (a) uses (more general than the dyadic pairs of the first draft; the reviewer's observation); in (b) the coarse grid is dyadic, as lem:tube-localized-discrepancy needs. In (b), \(\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\) and \(N\) large: (a) at \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\); \(P\ge1\): \(k\ge0\) in the tube lemma, whose tube width is then at most \(1\). In (c), the pair \((4,4)\), the cost at most \(2\) and \(y\ge2e^{16}\): lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c), the bound \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T\) and \(T\le4\); nesting: the increments are multiples of \(y\delta_0\) and \(\mathrm{TV}(g)=y\delta_0\sum_kP_k\) (for layers that are not nested the second fails and \(\sum_kP_k\) is not controlled). In (d), \(K\le N^{1/7}\): the layers of perimeter below \(1\); \(\log K\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y/2))^{1/3}\): the term \(Ta^{3/4}\); the split at \(y=N^{1/3}\) is a choice, any exponent below \(\frac12\) serving with another power of \(K\). Conclusions: (a) for every grid function and every admissible pair of meshes at once; (b) for every union with \(P\ge1\); (c) and (d) for every nested chain on the dyadic grids between \(\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \(2^{-\ell_1}\), against Lebesgue measure.

Baseline. The plainest recorded bound for unions of cells below the Leighton–Shor mesh is lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a), \(L_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}P(A)\): it charges a cut cell by its count, \(\sqrt{2n_Ct}+t\approx8\sqrt{\mu\log N}\), \((\log N)^{5/4}\), so the fine part already costs \((\log N)^{3/4}\) per unit perimeter. Part (a) charges a cut cell by its variance, which isoperimetry bounds by \(N\ell_C^2\), and the fine part costs \(\sqrt{\log N}\) per unit of variation; the Leighton–Shor factor then comes only from the coarse averages, where tube localization lowers it to \((\log(2^{\ell_1}/P))^{3/4}\) for a set of large perimeter. For single layers at level \(y\), the record's lem:discrete-flow-bound (c) gives \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\min\{1+(\log y)^{1/4},(\log N/\log(y/2))^{1/4}\}\), up to \((\log N)^{1/8}\); (d) gives \(C_d\sqrt{N\log N}\) at every level.

Degenerate cases. (a) with \(W=\delta_0\): \(E_Wg=g\) and both sides vanish; \(g\) constant: \(\mathrm{TV}=0\) and \(F(g)=0\); one fine cell \(A\) inside the square: \(P=4\delta_0\) and the bound is \(4c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,\delta_0\ge4c_\kappa\kappa\log N\), the scale of one fine cell's fluctuation within its coarse cell, \(\sqrt{\mu/q}\) up to \(\sqrt{\log N}\). (b) with \(A\) empty or the square: \(P=0\), outside (b), and \(D=0\); \(A\) of the largest perimeter, about \(2/\delta_0\): the factor is \(5^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\) and the bound \(O(N/\kappa)\), weaker than the trivial \(N\). (c) with \(K=0\): \(g=0\); every layer of perimeter below \(1\): only the second term; \(y\ge N^{1/3}\): (d) uses lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) for the whole chain.

Nonvacuity. On the curve's parameters at \((4,4)\): the family \(\kappa=1\), \(\delta_0=2^{-\ell_1-1}\), \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\) satisfies the hypotheses of (a) and (b) for every \(N\) with \(\log N\ge16\): \(\delta_0\ge\frac12(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\ge\sqrt{\log N/N}\) exactly when \((\log N)^{1/4}\ge2\), and \((W/\delta_0)^2=4\le\log N\); at \(N=2^{32}\), \(\ell_1=12\), \(\delta_0=2^{-13}\ge7.2\cdot10^{-5}\approx\sqrt{\log N/N}\). Chains near fixed polynomial guide families

17 October 2026 · Working proof; dyadic grids, against Lebesgue measure · Guided chains. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: Another subfamily of the discrete class bounded; the goal's state in Where we stand is unchanged.

Question. The cut-cell variance entry bounded nested chains of at most \(\min(N^{1/7},\exp((\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y/2))^{1/3}))\) layers at the conjectured order and named as next attempt the chains of more layers, "by the gap-charged bound for their coarse averages" at the Leighton–Shor mesh, first on concentric closed curves each wiggling below its gap to the next. The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy; this entry asks whether a chain of any number of layers is at the conjectured order when each layer stays within a thin tube of a guide drawn from a small family, which is the concentric case with its guides made general.

Target form. The goal's form is the class bound for the cell-smeared \(\mu_X-\mu_Y\) on the reduction's grid; this entry works in the discrete \(X\)-term of grid functions against Lebesgue measure on dyadic grids, which by lem:smeared-y-term (b) bounds the goal's form only for the class functions whose cell averages are the chains considered; the reduction's grid is not dyadic.

Chosen. The chaining lead entry-2026-10-16-fourth-route-review:2, not the queue head sandpile-odometer-flow: its latest follow-up named the attempt this entry makes, it bears directly on conjugate-class-discrepancy, and this is its fourth entry in the spell, after which it rotates.

General statement. lem:guided-chain-bound: part (a) for every union of fine cells, every union of coarse cells as guide and every tube of dyadic cells of side between \(2^{-\ell_1}\) and \(1\) holding their difference; part (b) for every family of at most \(N^c\) unions of coarse cells fixed in advance, every \(c>0\); part (c) for every weighted sum of layers with such guides and tubes; part (d) for every nested chain at \((4,4)\) of such layers, whatever its number of layers, at every level \(y\ge2e^{16}\); all on dyadic grids of side between \(\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \(2^{-\ell_1}\).

Guided chains

Setting. As in the cut-cell variance entry: \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\), \(\ell_1\) the Leighton–Shor scale, \(\kappa>0\) fixed, \(\delta_0\) dyadic with \(\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\le\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\), \(D(g)=\sum_ig(X_i)-N\int g\), \(P\) the inner perimeter of a union of cells, \(c_\kappa=\sqrt{10+20/\kappa^2}+\frac5{3\kappa}\), \(L\) the constant of lem:tube-localized-discrepancy, \(\Phi_k=(2(\ell_1-k)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\). Fine cells have side \(\delta_0\), coarse cells side \(2^{-\ell_1}\), \(W\)-cells side \(W=2^{-k}\), \(0\le k\le\ell_1\). A nested chain at level \(y\) is \(g=y\delta_0\sum_{k\le K}1_{A_k}\), \(A_1\supseteq\dots\supseteq A_K\) unions of fine cells, \(P_k=P(A_k)\); its discrete cost at \((4,4)\) is \(\sum_e\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eg|/(2\delta_0))\), and \(T=8(\log(y/2))^{-1/4}\).

Statement. Fix \(c>0\) and, for each \(N\), a family \(\mathcal F_N\) of at most \(N^c\) unions of coarse cells, chosen before the points are drawn. With probability tending to one, for every such \(\delta_0\): (a) every union \(A\) of fine cells, every union \(S\) of coarse cells, every \(W=2^{-k}\in[2^{-\ell_1},1]\) and every set \(\mathcal T\) of \(W\)-cells whose union contains \(A\triangle S\) have \[|D(1_A)-D(1_S)|\le c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,P(A)+L\sqrt N\,\Phi_k\big(P(A)+P(S)+12W\#\mathcal T\big);\] (b) every \(S\in\mathcal F_N\) has \(|D(1_S)|\le P(S)\sqrt{(c+3)N\log N}+(c+3)\log N\); more generally, for every family of \(M_N\ge1\) unions of coarse cells fixed before the points are drawn, with probability tending to one each member has \(|D(1_S)|\le P(S)\sqrt{N(\log M_N+3\log N)}+\log M_N+3\log N\); (c) for every \(\beta>0\), every \(w\in[2^{-\ell_1},1]\) and every finite collection of unions \(A_k\) of fine cells with \(P(A_k)>0\), each with a guide \(S_k\in\mathcal F_N\), a dyadic \(W_k\in[2^{-\ell_1},w]\) and a set \(\mathcal T_k\) of \(W_k\)-cells containing \(A_k\triangle S_k\) such that \(P(S_k)+12W_k\#\mathcal T_k\le\beta P(A_k)\), and all real \(a_k\), \[\Big|D\Big(\sum_ka_k1_{A_k}\Big)\Big|\le C\sqrt N\big((2\log_2(w2^{\ell_1})+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\big)\sum_k|a_k|P(A_k),\qquad C=c_\kappa+L(1+\beta)+\beta\sqrt{c+3}+(c+3)/\kappa;\] (d) at \((4,4)\), a nested chain \(g=y\delta_0\sum_k1_{A_k}\) of such layers at level \(y\ge2e^{16}\) with discrete cost at most \(2\) has \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt N\,T\big((2\log_2(w2^{\ell_1})+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\big)\), whatever its number of layers, and so \(|D(g)|\le23C\sqrt{N\log N}\) for \(N\) large when moreover \(\log(w2^{\ell_1})\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y/2))^{1/3}\).

Proof. Events: those of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (its (a) at the coarse mesh, allowed for \(N\) large as \((2^{-\ell_1}/\delta_0)^2\le4\sqrt{\log N}/\kappa^2\le\log N\)), of lem:tube-localized-discrepancy and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor, and, for (b), the event below. (a) With \(H=E_{2^{-\ell_1}}1_A\), lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a) gives \(|D(1_A)-D(H)|\le c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,P(A)\). The coarse cell function \(F=H-1_S\) takes values in \([-1,1]\) and vanishes on every coarse cell \(Q\) outside the union of \(\mathcal T\): such a \(Q\) lies in a \(W\)-cell not in \(\mathcal T\) (the \(W\)-cells are unions of coarse cells), so \(Q\cap(A\triangle S)=\emptyset\), and as \(S\cap Q\) is \(Q\) or empty, \(H_Q=1_S(Q)\). lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (b) with \(j=\ell_1\) gives \(|D(F)|\le L\sqrt N\,\Phi_k\big(V^0_{\ell_1}(F)+4W\sum_{Q\in\mathcal G_k}(\max_QF^++\max_QF^-)\big)\). The inner part of \(V^0_{\ell_1}(F)\) is at most \(V^{\mathrm{in}}(H)+V^{\mathrm{in}}(1_S)\le P(A)+P(S)\), the first by the global Fubini count in the proof of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor; its boundary ring counts \(|F|\le1\) along the edges on \(\partial[0,1]^2\) of coarse cells inside the union of \(\mathcal T\), at most \(4W\) of such edges per \(W\)-cell (exactly \(4W\) for the one cell at \(W=1\), at most \(2W\) otherwise), so at most \(4W\#\mathcal T\); and the extra term is at most \(4W\cdot2\#\mathcal T\). So \(|D(F)|\le L\sqrt N\,\Phi_k(P(A)+P(S)+12W\#\mathcal T)\), and \(D(1_A)-D(1_S)=(D(1_A)-D(H))+D(F)\). (b) \(\#(X\cap S)\) is binomial \((N,p)\), \(p=\lambda(S)\). The relative isoperimetry of the cut-cell variance entry, applied to the unit square cut into coarse cells, gives \(p(1-p)\le\min(p,1-p)\le P(S)^2/2\), so the variance is at most \(NP(S)^2/2\); Bernstein's inequality with \(t=\log M_N+3\log N\) gives \(|D(1_S)|\le P(S)\sqrt{Nt}+t/3\) except with probability \(2e^{-t}=2N^{-3}/M_N\), and the union over the \(M_N\) members, fixed before the points, fails with probability at most \(2N^{-3}\); \(M_N\le N^c\) gives the first form (no union over \(\delta_0\) is needed, as \(S\) does not depend on it). (c) By linearity \(D(\sum_ka_k1_{A_k})=\sum_ka_kD(1_{A_k})\). For each layer, (a) with \(W_k=2^{-k_k}\le w\), so \(\ell_1-k_k\le\log_2(w2^{\ell_1})\), and (b) give \(|D(1_{A_k})|\le c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,P_k+L(1+\beta)\sqrt N\,\Phi_wP_k+\beta\sqrt{(c+3)N\log N}\,P_k+(c+3)\log N\), with \(P_k=P(A_k)\) and \(\Phi_w=(2\log_2(w2^{\ell_1})+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\); as \(P_k>0\) forces \(P_k\ge\delta_0\), \((c+3)\log N\le\frac{c+3}\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,P_k\). Summing with the weights \(|a_k|\), and \(\sqrt{\log N}\le\Phi_w\), gives (c). (d) Layers with \(P_k=0\) are empty or the whole square and contribute \(0\). As in lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (c), nesting gives \(\mathrm{TV}(g)=y\delta_0\sum_kP_k\), and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) gives \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T\); (c) with \(a_k=y\delta_0\) gives the first bound. For the second, with \(x=\log(w2^{\ell_1})\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y/2))^{1/3}\), \(2\log_2(w2^{\ell_1})=2.885x\), and \((a+b)^{3/4}\le a^{3/4}+b^{3/4}\): \(T(2.885x+5)^{3/4}\le8(\log(y/2))^{-1/4}\big(2.22(\log N)^{1/2}(\log(y/2))^{1/4}+5^{3/4}\big)\le17.8\sqrt{\log N}+13.4\), as \((\log(y/2))^{-1/4}\le\frac12\); with \(T\sqrt{\log N}\le4\sqrt{\log N}\) and \(13.4\le\sqrt{\log N}\) for \(\log N\ge180\), the bracket times \(T\) is at most \(23\sqrt{\log N}\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Independence and uniformity of the points: the binomial count in (b) and the events of the cited lemmas. \(\delta_0\) dyadic between \(\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \(2^{-\ell_1}\): lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a) at the coarse mesh and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c). \(S\) a union of coarse cells: \(F\) is a cell function of the coarse mesh, as the tube lemma needs, and the relative isoperimetry in (b); \(W\ge2^{-\ell_1}\) dyadic: the tube lemma's \(k\le j=\ell_1\) and the \(W\)-cells as unions of coarse cells. \(\mathcal F_N\) fixed before the points are drawn and of at most \(N^c\) members: the union bound in (b), whose event depends on the family, so the family is fixed before the event; a guide chosen after the points from a larger family is not covered, and (c) uses (b) only through its bound, so any guide satisfying that bound would serve. In (c), \(P(S_k)+12W_k\#\mathcal T_k\le\beta P_k\): to charge the guide and tube terms to the layer's own perimeter; \(W_k\le w\): the factor; \(P(A_k)>0\): the additive \(\log N\) charged to \(P_k\ge\delta_0\); (c) uses neither nesting, nor a level, nor the pair (the reviewer's observation; the first draft stated it for nested chains at \((4,4)\) only, less general than its proof). In (d), the pair \((4,4)\), the cost and \(y\ge2e^{16}\): lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c); nesting: \(\mathrm{TV}(g)=y\delta_0\sum_kP_k\); and for the second bound the condition on \(w\) and \(\log N\ge180\). Conclusions: (a) for every union and every guide and tube; (b) for every member of the family; (c) for every weighted sum of guided layers; (d) for every guided nested chain at \((4,4)\), of any number of layers, against Lebesgue measure.

Baseline. For a chain of \(K\) layers the plainest recorded bounds are lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b), \(L_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}T\), the full factor, and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (c), \(C_b\sqrt NT(2\log_2(Ky^2)+5)^{3/4}\), which is the full factor once \(K\) is polynomial in \(N\); lem:discrete-flow-bound (c) charges chains of multiplicity \(m\) at \(C\sqrt{N\log N}(1+(\log(my))^{1/4})\). For the difference between a layer and its guide, the count that needs no idea is Bernstein in each tube cell with a union over the \(2^{(W/\delta_0)^2}\) unions of its fine cells: \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\,W\#\mathcal T\) when \(W2^{\ell_1}\) is bounded, which with (b) already decides chains with \(w2^{\ell_1}=O(1)\), and a loss of a factor of order \(W2^{\ell_1}\) beyond, where (a) loses \((\log(W2^{\ell_1}))^{3/4}\). Part (c) charges a guided chain by the tube width alone, whatever \(K\): the guides carry the large scales, which (b) charges at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) through a union bound over the family, and the layers' departures from their guides carry only the scales below \(w\).

Degenerate cases. (a) with \(A=S\) a union of coarse cells and \(\mathcal T\) empty: \(D(1_A)-D(1_S)=0\), while the bound is \(c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,P(S)+2L\sqrt N\Phi_kP(S)\), true and weaker; with \(W=1\), one \(W\)-cell with \(4W\) of the square's boundary: \(\Phi_0\) is the full factor and the bound adds \(12\) to the perimeters, the plainest coarse bound. (b) with \(S\) empty or the square: \(P(S)=0\) and \(D(1_S)=0\le(c+3)\log N\). (c) with \(K=0\): \(g=0\); with every guide equal to its layer (layers unions of coarse cells, \(\mathcal T_k\) empty, \(\beta=1\)): the chain is charged at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) per unit of variation when the layers lie in the family, and \(w=2^{-\ell_1}\) gives the factor \(5^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\).

Nonvacuity. On the curve's parameters at \((4,4)\): \(\kappa=1\), \(\delta_0=2^{-\ell_1-1}\) (in range once \(\log N\ge16\)), \(y=y_N=e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\) (at least \(2e^{16}\) once \(\log N\ge281\)), \(\mathcal F_N\) the rectangles that are unions of coarse cells (at most \(2^{4\ell_1}\le N^2\), so \(c=2\)), and the tube side \(w=W_k=2^{r-\ell_1}\) with \(r=\lceil\log_2\log N\rceil\), so \(\log N\le w2^{\ell_1}<2\log N\). Guides \(S_k=[a_k,1-a_k]^2\), \(a_k=3kw\), unions of coarse cells, side \(s_k=1-2a_k\ge\frac12\) for \(k\le1/(12w)\); \(A_k=S_k\cup R_k\), where \(R_k\) is the union of the fine cells of the ring \(\{x\notin S_k:\mathrm{dist}_\infty(x,S_k)<w\}\) that lie within \(\infty\)-distance \(h_k\) of \(S_k\), \(h_k\) a fine-grid staircase along \(\partial S_k\) rising and falling between \(\delta_0\) and \(w-\delta_0\) with slope one; \(\mathcal T_k\) the \(w\)-cells of the ring, \(\#\mathcal T_k=4s_k/w+4\). The outer boundary of \(R_k\) is a staircase of slope one, of length \(2\) per unit along \(\partial S_k\) up to the corners, so \(7s_k\le8s_k-16w\le P_k\le8s_k+16w\) for \(N\) large; \(P(S_k)+12w\#\mathcal T_k=52s_k+48w\le53s_k\le8P_k\), \(\beta=8\). The ring of \(S_{k+1}\) lies in \([a_k+2w,1-a_k-2w]^2\subset S_k\), so \(A_{k+1}\subseteq S_k\subseteq A_k\), and the boundaries lie in disjoint rings, one through each edge. The cost is \(\delta_0\psi_4^*(y/2)\sum_kP_k\le9K\delta_0\psi_4^*(y/2)\), at most \(2\) for \(K\le K_N=\min(\lfloor2/(9\delta_0\psi_4^*(y/2))\rfloor,\lfloor1/(12w)\rfloor)\); with \(\psi_4^*(y/2)\le e^{\sqrt{\log N}}(\log N)^{1/8}\) and \(1/(12w)\ge2^{\ell_1}/(24\log N)\), \(K_N\) is of order \(N^{1/2-o(1)}\), so \(\log K_N>(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y/2))^{1/3}=(\log N)^{5/6}\) and \(K_N>N^{1/7}\) for \(N\) large, while \(\log(w2^{\ell_1})\le\log\log N+1\) meets (d)'s condition. At this chain lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) does not apply and its (c) gives the factor \((2\log_2(K_Ny^2)+5)^{3/4}\), of order \((\log N)^{3/4}\); lem:discrete-flow-bound (c) (multiplicity one, from \(\log N\ge4096\)) gives \(C\sqrt{N\log N}(\log N)^{1/8}\); (d) gives \(C\sqrt NT((2r+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})=O(\sqrt{N\log N}(\log N)^{-1/8})\), and here the tube factor \((2r+5)^{3/4}\) is of order \((\log\log N)^{3/4}\). Plainest bound. For one fixed chain, Bernstein's inequality for \(D(g)\), with variance at most \(N(y\delta_0K_N)^2\) and \(y\delta_0K_N\le\frac{2y}{9\psi_4^*(y/2)}\le\frac T9\) (as \(\psi_4^*(u)\ge\frac12u(\log u)^{1/4}\)), gives at most \(T\sqrt{N\log N}/6\): a fixed witness is decided by a bound for one function, and the statement's content is its uniformity, over every guided chain with these tubes (at most \(\exp(O(\sum_kP_k/\delta_0))\) of them) and over every guided collection. The plainest uniform bound for the tube terms, Bernstein in each \(w\)-cell of \(\mathcal T_k\) with a union over the \(2^{(w/\delta_0)^2}\) unions of its fine cells, charges about \(\sqrt N\,w/\delta_0\approx2\sqrt N\log N\) per unit of tube length, as \((w/\delta_0)^2\approx4(\log N)^2\) exceeds \(\log N\): above the conjectured order, where (a) charges \((\log\log N)^{3/4}\sqrt N\); at \(w=2^{-\ell_1}\), the first draft's witness, that count already decides the tube terms (the reviewer's observation), and (a) adds nothing there.

(1) A reply said a prevention for a commit sent before its edit's result would be built "in the next cycle": partly wrong, since the build failed-edit-commit-check had been queued with its reason, but the reply did not name it, and a promise is not a queued item. (2) Two hook notices answered "Read the item" before their items were read: right; tools/hook_notices.py now refuses an answer that does not quote eight consecutive words of the item's queued text, and both exposing answers are refused (research/provenance/framework/notice-quote-20261017.txt). (3) A commit message left without two conditions of its claim after the hook warned: right; the entry states both, and messages are not amended once the base has moved; a refusal before the fast-forward is queued as commit-qualifier-before-ff, not built because the warning lists 57 conditions over 33 registry-changing commits of the last 200 (research/provenance/framework/commit-qualifier-replay-20261017.txt), so its false refusals must be counted first. Meta. The stand-in review's right objections share one way of working: acting on a name in place of the thing it names, an item answered from its identifier, a session named from a pattern, a message committed and its warning left for later.
